title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Members of the Board. Subject to Blackout Periods, the hedging ban on retention-locked/unvested securities, and encouraged (not mandatory) prior notification plus mandatory post-trade notice to the Company Secretary for ASX reporting. Not named in the express security-interest/margin-loan consent clause or the short-term/speculative trading ban.

tiers.name: Officers
tiers.description: An employee who reports to the Managing Director, a Director, or any other employee so designated by the Managing Director. Subject to Blackout Periods, the hedging ban, a ban on short-term or speculative trading, and a requirement for the Chairman's written consent before granting any security interest (including a margin loan) over Nick Scali securities they own.

tiers.name: all other employees
tiers.description: Employees who are neither Directors nor Officers. Subject to Blackout Periods and the hedging ban; not named in the short-term trading ban or the security-interest consent requirement, and the Connected Entity concept does not extend to them.

tiers.name: Connected Entities
tiers.description: Any trust, company or other entity that a Director or Officer controls in relation to Nick Scali Limited securities. Directors/Officers must take all reasonable steps to ensure their Connected Entity complies with the policy; an exemption applies to a trust where the Director/Officer is not a beneficiary, is not sole trustee, and the trust's dealing decisions are made independently of them.

exemption_authority: Approval to trade during a Blackout Period is granted only in exceptional personal circumstances (severe financial hardship or other circumstances the Chairman deems exceptional) by the role-specific approver (Chairman for Directors, Deputy Chairman for the Chairman, Audit & Risk Committee Chairman for the Deputy Chairman, Managing Director for Officers), valid for 7 days. There is no separate exemption route described for the Officer-specific security-interest/margin-loan consent requirement or the short-term/speculative trading ban, which sit outside the Blackout Period regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Officers and Connected Entities must not grant a security interest over Nick Scali securities they own, including any margin loan without first receiving the written consent of the Chairman.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar for an Officer is only possible with the Chairman's prior written consent to the security interest over the collared shares; the clause does not on its face extend to Directors.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Nick Scali Directors, Officers and employees must not enter into a transaction that is designated or intended to hedge that employee’s exposure to the Nick Scali security that is subject to retention arrangements or an unvested Nick Scali option.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging ban, and therefore the collar's put/call legs, only bites on unvested or retention-locked securities; hedging fully vested, unrestricted shares is not expressly prohibited, which is the state a funded collar would target.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Officers and Connected Entities must not grant a security interest over Nick Scali securities they own, including any margin loan without first receiving the written consent of the Chairman.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because Directors are not named in this clause, a Director's secured loan against vested shares is not addressed by any express prohibition or consent requirement in the policy, unlike an Officer's.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Officers and Connected Entities must not engage in short-term or speculative trading in Nick Scali securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An Officer's collar should be structured with sufficient tenor and a clear non-speculative rationale to avoid characterisation as short-term or speculative trading; this restriction does not apply to Directors on its face.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Officers are encouraged to give prior notification to the Company Secretary of any proposed dealing in Nick Scali Limited’s securities. Directors and Officers are to advise the Company Secretary as soon as possible after a trade has occurred.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Outside Blackout Periods there is no mandatory pre-clearance system for Directors or Officers, only mandatory post-trade notice (to support ASX Appendix 3Y reporting for Directors), which eases execution timing for a collar entered in an open window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: each Director or Officer must take all reasonable steps to ensure that their Connected Entity complies with this Policy in relation to Nick Scali Limited Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the security-interest consent requirement or the hedging ban, since Connected Entities are directly bound and the Director/Officer must ensure their compliance.

summary: A funded collar is plausible for a Director over fully vested, unrestricted shares: the hedging ban applies only to securities under retention arrangements or unvested options, and Directors are not named in the clause requiring consent before granting a security interest, so neither leg is expressly prohibited for them, subject to dealing outside Blackout Periods (or under a 7-day exceptional-circumstances approval from the Chairman/Deputy Chairman/Audit & Risk Chair) and outside possession of inside information. For an Officer, the same hedging carve-out likely permits the put/call legs over vested-unrestricted shares, but the loan leg requires the Chairman's prior written consent because Officers (and their Connected Entities) may not grant a security interest, including a margin loan, over shares they own without it; Officers must also avoid the arrangement reading as short-term or speculative trading. The policy does not address forced sale by a secured lender during a Blackout Period, minimum shareholding requirements, or any ongoing disclosure of financing arrangements, so those points would need to be addressed contractually with the bank. Outside Blackout Periods, notification to the Company Secretary is only encouraged (not mandatory) before dealing, though post-trade notice is required for Directors and Officers.
